title: Dynamic Analysis of Your Own Program: Debuggers, Traces, and Confirming Static Claims

questions.question: You set breakpoints on bump, classify, and sum_balances in a build of your own program, run it to completion, and every breakpoint reports hit count = 0. What does that run prove?
options: That the program has no functions
That no out-of-line copy of the three functions ran for this input in this build, and nothing about other inputs or other builds
That the breakpoints were set at the wrong addresses
The three functions are dead code and can be removed
questions.explanation: A hit count is an observation about one execution of one build. At -O2 the compiler inlined the three functions and folded the results into constants, so the exported copies never ran. The functions are still in the symbol table.

questions.question: At the bump breakpoint lldb prints x0 = 0x16fdfe008, x1 = 0x5, and memory read -s4 -fx -c8 $x0 prints 0x00000073 0x000000fa 0x00000009 0x00000000 0x00000000 0x3ff40000 0x00000719 0x00000001. Which static claim does the second word confirm?
options: That balance is at offset 4 and holds 250, the value DWARF puts at DW_AT_data_member_location 0x04
That rate is a float
That x1 holds the struct pointer
That the struct is 16 bytes long
questions.explanation: The words are the struct bytes starting at a. Word 1 sits at offset 4, holds 0xfa = 250, and matches frame variable a->balance. Words 4 and 5 are the IEEE-754 double 1.25 at offset 16, and words 6 and 7 are the label pointer at offset 24.

questions.question: In classify at -O0 the first conditional branch is tbz w8, #0x1f, 0x100000504 with the fall-through at 0x1000004f4. The run stops at 0x1000004f4 for an account with balance -40. Is the lesson 33 edge claim confirmed or refuted?
options: Refuted, because the branch to 0x100000504 was not taken
Confirmed, because tbz branches when bit 31 is zero, so a negative balance falls through to the return -1 block exactly as the lifted condition predicts
Not observed, because tbz is not a conditional branch
Refuted, because -40 is less than 200
questions.explanation: tbz is test bit and branch if zero. Bit 31 of -40 is set, so the branch is not taken and execution falls through. The static claim says the taken edge is for balance >= 0 and the fall-through edge is for balance < 0, which is what the stop shows.

questions.question: watchpoint set variable a->balance reports size = 4, type = m, and watchpoint list prints Number of supported hardware watchpoints: 4. Why does lldb report a count at all?
options: Because macOS allows only four debuggers at once
Because data watchpoints use per-core debug registers, DR0 to DR3 on x86-64 and DBGWVR/DBGWCR pairs on arm64, so a fixed number of them exist and a wide region can use more than one
Because watchpoints are implemented in software and lldb limits them to keep the process fast
Because the count is the number of bytes watched
questions.explanation: Hardware watchpoints compare every memory access against a small set of address registers. x86-64 has four, arm64 implementations have between 2 and 64, and this machine reports 4. When the slots run out lldb refuses the next watchpoint.

questions.question: You saved a core with process save-core --style stack at the bump breakpoint. Loading it with lldb -c shows balance = 250 but label = "" with the pointer 0x100000719 intact. What happened?
options: lldb cannot print strings from core files
The core is corrupt
The program never set label
The string lives in the __TEXT segment of the executable, which a stack-style core does not include, so the pointer is present and the bytes behind it are not
questions.explanation: A stack-style core saves the stack and modified memory, 49152 bytes here. The literal "savings" is read-only data in the binary. lldb warns that such a core may not show binaries, and --style full includes all process memory.

questions.question: On Apple silicon, why does clang -g -o account account.c produce a binary that lldb can debug without any extra signing step?
options: Because the Command Line Tools disable System Integrity Protection

Because the linker ad-hoc signs arm64 output by default (flags adhoc,linker-signed), the binary is not hardened, and it has no entitlements, so Apple's rule that the target must opt out of debugging does not apply
Because lldb ignores code signatures
Because the binary carries the com.apple.security.cs.debugger entitlement
questions.explanation: codesign -dvvv shows Signature=adhoc and flags=0x20002(adhoc,linker-signed) with no entitlements. The debugger side is covered by debugserver, which Apple signed with its own private entitlements. Only a hardened binary without get-task-allow refuses the task port.

questions.question: Which statement about record-and-replay with rr is correct for a learner on an Apple silicon Mac?
options: rr works inside Docker on macOS because Docker runs Linux
rr replaces lldb on macOS since 5.9.0
rr runs on macOS and records with dtrace
rr is Linux only, needs hardware performance counters, and no virtualization on macOS exposes them, so the only path is a Linux machine or a VM elsewhere with counter virtualization enabled
questions.explanation: rr records on Linux with perf counters on Intel, AMD Zen, or certain AArch64 cores including Apple M-series under Linux. Its own wiki says no virtualization on macOS supports performance counter virtualization, which rules out Docker and Colima VMs on this machine.
